newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-GERMANY WIN MEN'S 4X100 FREESTYLE RELAY.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-GERMANY WIN MEN'S 4X100 FREESTYLE RELAY.

text.p: Germany denied Sweden an emotional victory on Sunday in the men's 4x100 metres freestyle relay on the final day of the world short-course swimming championships.
The race marked the competitive farewell of Sweden's Anders Holmertz, winner of two Olympic silvers and a bronze in individual freestyle races.
Holmertz, swimming the second leg, took over in fourth place and moved Sweden up to third with a personal 100 metres split of 48.84 seconds.
Australia led over the first two legs of the race thanks to Michael Klim and Scott Logan but Alexander Luederitz pushed Germany just in front on the third leg, with Sweden still third.
Lars Frolunder gave furious chase to the leaders on the anchor leg for Sweden, overhauled Australia's Jeffrey English but could not quite catch Germany's Aimo Heilmann.
Brazil touched third but were disqualified for a premature start by their second swimmer.
Germany won in three minutes 14.08 seconds, with Sweden second -- one more silver for Holmertz -- in 3:14.22 and Australia third in 3:14.83.
